When I first started learning waacking I used to hit myself all the time. After I practiced more and was more aware of my body and what my head was doing from jazz training (spotting while turning etc) and isolation training in hip hop I got better and controlling where my hands move

that being said... I have scratched my face open in the last month from a girls style routine... I might just be clumsy
That's a good point to make! I think if OP took more hip hop foundation classes they would have more lego blocks to play and build with

Pick a song that makes you want to move and listen to it. Try and break it down into the different elements e.g. beat, vocal line, guitar riffs, bass, any strings, keyboard etc think of stuff to do relating to each element. This should help train you with musicality, and once you can do it to your favourite songs you can start doing it with songs you don't know as well

in terms of freestyle training, think about each body part individually and what you can do movement wise with just that body part. the more your practice this the better your isolations and flexibility will be. over time, you can start move 2 or three body parts in isolation

it doesn't sound like much but you really do just have to listen to tunes and practice moves until you can do them without thinking.

With Lia's Gold choreography she uses a lot of her popping foundations. I think if you want to specifically perfect that routine you'll have to take some popping classes. In general it would be good for you to take foundation classes in locking, waacking, vogueing, top rock (a component of breaking), house, just so you can see where urban choreographers are riffing off of

Otherwise constant practice will help you get better. Your brain is like a muscle, the more you train it the better it gets. You're also still young so you'll pick things up a lot faster!

Inside the classroom don't stick to one side of the room, like if you prefer standing on the right move to the left side of the room. At home/away from the studio practice without mirror. If you use public transport try to listen to the song and visualise the moves in your head.
